title: How Your Body Cools Itself in Extreme Heat
description: How sweating cools you, who is most at risk and why heat stroke is an emergency, from NIH and CDC.
narration: How does your body stay cool on a hot day? Your body has a built-in cooling system, and sweating is the key. As sweat dries, it carries heat away from the skin. If sweating is not enough, you risk hyperthermia, a heat-related illness. Older people, young children and people who are ill are especially at risk. In heat stroke, the sweating mechanism fails and the body temperature rises rapidly. It is a medical emergency. Air conditioning is the best protection against hyperthermia.
